blocks.title: Compound and simple interest on £10,000 at 7% over 30 years
blocks.subtitle: Compounding ends at £76,123 against £31,000 for simple interest at the same rate.
blocks.lede: Two savers contribute the same total at the same rate; the earlier one ends ahead.
blocks.author: Worked example

blocks.title: How one period of compounding is calculated
blocks.lede: Simple interest adds. Compound interest multiplies. Everything else follows from that one difference.

blocks.title: The three steps in a single compounding period

steps.title: Start with a balance
steps.text: Whatever you already hold at the beginning of the period.

steps.title: Apply the rate
steps.text: Interest is calculated on the whole balance, not on the original deposit.

steps.title: Add it back
steps.text: The interest joins the balance, so next period it earns interest too.

blocks.title: Step three is the entire mechanism
blocks.text: Step three is the entire mechanism. Remove it and compound interest becomes simple interest.

blocks.title: Balance over 30 years at 7%, compounded and simple
blocks.subtitle: £10,000 initial deposit. The gap comes from step three repeating, not from the rate.
blocks.note: Both lines share one axis. Two y-scales here would invent a relationship the arithmetic does not contain.

items.label: Difference
items.note: All of it created by re-investing the interest.

blocks.title: The effect of starting age on the final balance
blocks.lede: Time enters the formula as an exponent. Contributions enter it as a multiplier. Exponents win.

left.label: Saver A
left.headline: Pays in for 10 years, then stops

right.label: Saver B
right.headline: Pays in for 30 years, and never stops

blocks.note: Saver A contributes a third as much and still finishes ahead.

blocks.title: How an annual fee reduces the final balance
blocks.lede: The same exponent that builds the balance also magnifies anything subtracted every year.

blocks.title: The cost of a 1% fee over 30 years
blocks.note: One percent a year removes roughly a quarter of the balance.

blocks.title: Method
items: All figures assume a constant 7% nominal annual return, compounded annually, with no tax.
Contributions are modelled as made at the end of each year.
Fee scenario applies a flat 1% of balance annually before compounding.
